steps.what: Stake outer ring to FT1 to FT4 from the BCLS offsets; nail outer boards to stakes, set to the pour line, spreaders every 1.2 m.
steps.gate: Footing forms: line +-25 mm, top +-13 mm (typical spec, ACI 117-style)
steps.app: Scan any board: side, pour line height, neighbours

steps.what: Inner ring with keyway strip; check diagonals against the model (design diagonal difference 0.2 mm).
steps.app: Level tab: slope / plumb check; Log tab photo per side

steps.what: Pour to the burned line; strike; strip forms; wall pour with rented panel forms (not cut by Acucut).
steps.gate: Foundation wall line +-13 mm, top +-6 mm
steps.app: Bundles: forms returned or reused as blocking

steps.what: Lay PT sill plates on gasket; drill at the burned bolt centres; set bolts or template; fix.
steps.gate: 9.23.6.1 spacing and diameter; sill line +-10 mm, level +-3 mm
steps.app: Scan the sill, the next framing step opens

benefits.value: 20 bolt centres marked on 6 sill plates, every spacing <= 2.4 m
benefits.detail: Generated by this script from the 28 m perimeter; code spacing and diameter per rule FRM-ANC-001 (BCBC 9.23.6.1). High-seismic sites (Smax over 0.47, FRM-ANC-002) need closer bolts per Table 9.23.6.1: set per site.

benefits.value: 2.6 h less measuring and marking on 78 pieces (est.)
benefits.detail: Assumes 2 min per piece for tape, pencil and cut on site versus a labelled pick. The pour line also removes a string line and level pass per side.

benefits.value: Form line +-25 mm and wall top +-6 mm are the spec gates in the stake-out job
benefits.detail: Gate values in stakeout_job.json (typical residential practice). The simulated footing phase passed with max horizontal error 21.2 mm; foundation phase flagged at 9.9 mm vs 13 mm and 6 mm vertical.

benefits.value: 6.1% cut waste vs 10% typical order allowance
benefits.detail: Acucut 1D nester on this trade's 78 sticks: 32 boards, 140.82 m stock for 132.2 m of parts (bundle-window constrained runs add about 0.5 points). Conventional allowance 5 to 15% (BuildingScience). Difference about 22 bf, CAD 16 at CAD 700/MBF (estimate).

FMI puts rework at about 5% of construction spend and 48% of rework on poor communication or data. If labelled, sequenced, pre-checked parts prevent 15 to 30% of this trade's rework (estimate), callbacks fall by 0.75 to 1.50% of trade spend. On the NAHB reference home (US$428,215 build, 10.0% share = US$42,822) that is US$321 to US$642; not scaled to the 96 m2 sample. Foundation errors are the most expensive to fix; this figure is the generic rework rate, not a foundation-specific study.

cell_does: Cuts footing form boards (2x10), inner and outer rings, to the footing ring (outer 8.3 x 6.3 m, inner 7.3 x 5.3 m) with 45-degree mitres where the ring is closed.
Burns a pour line at design footing thickness (200 mm) along every form board, so the crew strikes to a line rather than a tape.
Cuts 2x2 form stakes and 2x4 spreaders (50 cm footing width) and 2x4 keyway strips to length, bundled per side.
Cuts PT 2x6 sill plates and burns anchor-bolt centres (12.7 mm bolt, 14.3 mm hole by practice) at 2.4 m o.c. at most, 250 mm from each end (BCBC 9.23.6.1).
cell_cannot: Rebar: cut, bent and placed by the rebar supplier. Out of scope for the cell; the takeoff only lists lengths for them.
Wall forms beyond lumber: most BC basement walls use rented reusable panel forms; Acucut cuts the lumber walers, bulkheads, bucks and ledger pieces around them, not the panels.
Drill the anchor-bolt holes (needs a drill head, an add-on) or place and float the bolts; the burned centre is for the crew's drill or template.
Laser-mark pressure-treated lumber unreviewed: preservative-laden smoke is a hazard until the extractor and SDS are reviewed. Default for PT is a QR on the end grain tag and a reviewed trial.
Permanent wood foundations (CSA S406): cutting PT studs and plates is possible, but the PWF fastener, sheathing and drainage schedule belongs to the PWF designer.

addons.name: Drill head on the saw carriage
addons.why: Pre-drills sill plates at the burned centres (cell core only marks).

addons.name: Panel saw option
addons.why: Plywood form faces, sheathing and closure panels.

app: Build: foundation steps ahead of the framing steps; Bundles: 4 form bundles + the sill pallet with drop zones.
Scan: board or sill gives its side, the burned pour line, bolt centres and tolerance for that phase (pad, footing, wall, sill).
Site: footing and pad rings on the terrain; as-built over-dig map from the excavation run.
refs: BCBC 9.15 footings and foundations; 9.23.6.1 anchorage; 9.23.7.1 sill plates; 9.23.2.3 wood/concrete separation
Rebar by supplier: out of scope
code: BCBC 9.15 (footings and foundations), 9.23.6 (anchorage), 9.23.7 (sill plates), 9.12; CSA S406 for permanent wood foundations; CSA A23.1 concrete
summary: Footing form boards with a laser-burned pour line, stakes, spreaders and keyway strips, plus pressure-treated sill plates with anchor-bolt positions burned at 2.4 m centres or less.
highlight: 20 anchor-bolt centres pre-marked on PT sills, footing forms with the pour line burned, 6.1% form-lumber waste.
routing: Acucut routing: the cell's nester groups this trade's parts by section and stock length, cuts them in bundle order (last-installed at the bottom), laser-burns the label, QR and every mark listed, and drops each bundle in its zone so the crew picks in install order.
